items.informal_name: Supremum Upper Bound Lemma for Finite Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [inst : SemilatticeSup α] {s : Finset β} (f : β → α) {a : α} {b : β} (hb : b ∈ s),
  a ≤ f b → a ≤ s.sup' ⋯ f
items.informal_description: Given a non-empty finite set $ s $ of elements in type $ \beta $, a function $ f : \beta \to \alpha $ where $ \alpha $ is a sup-semilattice with bottom element $ \bot $, and an element $ a \in \alpha $, if there exists $ b \in s $ such that $ a \leq f(b) $, then $ a $ is less than or equal to the supremum of $ f $ over $ s $, denoted $ \sup'_{x \in s} f(x) $.

items.informal_name: Supremum of Finite Set is Less Than $ a $ iff All Elements Are Less Than $ a $
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder α] {a : α} {s : Set ι} {f : ι → α},
  s.Finite → (∃ x ∈ s, sSup ∅ ≤ f x) → (⨆ i ∈ s, f i < a ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, f x < a)
items.informal_description: For a non-empty finite set $ s $ in a conditionally complete lattice $ \alpha $ and a function $ f : \iota \to \alpha $, if there exists an $ x \in s $ such that $ \sup \emptyset \leq f(x) $, then $ \sup_{x \in s} f(x) < a $ if and only if $ f(x) < a $ for all $ x \in s $.

items.informal_name: Supremum of a Finite Set Bounds Its Elements
items.type: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [Finite ι] [inst : ConditionallyCompleteLattice α] (f : ι → α) (i : ι), f i ≤ ⨆ j, f j
items.informal_description: In a conditionally complete lattice, for any finite index set $\iota$ and function $f : \iota \to \alpha$, each element $f(i)$ satisfies $f(i) \leq \sup_{j \in \iota} f(j)$.

items.informal_name: Characterization of Supremum in Non-Empty Finite Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_5} [inst : LinearOrder α] {s : Finset ι} (H : s.Nonempty) {f : ι → α} {a : α},
  a ≤ s.sup' H f ↔ ∃ b ∈ s, a ≤ f b
items.informal_description: For any element $ a $ in a sup-semilattice $ \alpha $ with a bottom element, and for any non-empty finite set $ s $ of elements in $ \beta $, the inequality $ a \leq \sup_{b \in s} f(b) $ holds if and only if there exists an element $ b \in s $ such that $ a \leq f(b) $.

items.informal_name: Supremum of Function over Non-Empty Finite Set in Sup-Semilattice with Bottom
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [inst : SemilatticeSup α] {s : Finset β} (f : β → α) {b : β} (h : b ∈ s),
  f b ≤ s.sup' ⋯ f
items.informal_description: Given a non-empty finite set $ s $ of elements of type $ \beta $ and a function $ f : \beta \to \alpha $ where $ \alpha $ is a sup-semilattice with a bottom element $ \bot $, the supremum of $ f(x) $ for all $ x \in s $ is computed by starting from $ \bot $ and iteratively applying the supremum operation $ \sqcup $. Since $ s $ is non-empty, the result is guaranteed to be an element of $ \alpha $ (not $ \bot $).

items.informal_name: Supremum Characterization via Element Existence in Finite Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_5} [inst : LinearOrder α] [inst_1 : OrderBot α] {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → α} {a : α},
  ⊥ < a → (a ≤ s.sup f ↔ ∃ b ∈ s, a ≤ f b)
items.informal_description: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered distributive lattice with a bottom element $\bot$, and let $f : \beta \to \alpha$ be a function. For any finite set $s \subseteq \beta$ and any element $a \in \alpha$ with $a > \bot$, it holds that $a \leq \sup_{b \in s} f(b)$ if and only if there exists an element $b \in s$ such that $a \leq f(b)$.
